prompt: In 120 to 180 words, compare ranking metrics and classification metrics in exactly four numbered points. Include one search-system example and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.

turns.user_message: In 120 to 180 words, compare ranking metrics and classification metrics in exactly four numbered points. Include one search-system example and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.
turns.assistant_message:
1. Ranking metrics evaluate the order of items (e.g., documents, products) based on relevance, focusing on how well top results match user intent; classification metrics assess discrete label predictions (e.g., spam vs. not spam) by measuring correctness across all instances.  
2. Ranking metrics like NDCG or MAP reward placing highly relevant items early in the list, penalizing irrelevant results even if overall accuracy is high; classification metrics like accuracy or F1-score treat all errors equally, regardless of rank or position.  
3. Ranking is inherently list-sensitive and context-dependent — ideal for search or recommendation systems where user attention decays with position; classification assumes independent, unordered instances suited to tasks like medical diagnosis or image tagging.  
4. For example, in a web search engine, NDCG@10 measures how well the top 10 results satisfy a query by weighting relevance by position, whereas classification metrics would incorrectly treat retrieving the 10th relevant document as equally good as retrieving it first.  
Conclusion: Ranking metrics optimize for user experience in ordered outputs, while classification metrics optimize for correctness in discrete labeling tasks.
